The gradient observation has conditionally zero-mean noise with bounded conditional second moment and vanishing bias.
The steps satisfy \(a_k>0\), \(\sum_k a_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k a_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iterate remains in \(X\), and under boundedness and the usual projected-flow stability condition, limit points satisfy \(0\in\nabla f(x)+N_X(x)\) almost surely.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\in X\). If the iterates are almost surely bounded and the internally chain-transitive sets of those dynamics consist only of equilibria, all accumulation points obey this constrained first-order condition almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project every noisy gradient step onto the closed convex feasible set; stable limit points satisfy the constrained first-order stationarity condition.

children.title: Primal-Dual Stochastic Approximation
children.top_down_role: Coupled simulation-based adaptation of decision variables and dual variables.

assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\leq0\), with closed convex \(X\) and differentiable convex \(f,g_i\).
The simulation estimators of \(\nabla_x L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) and \(g(x_k)\) have martingale-difference noise, bounded conditional second moments, and vanishing bias.
The positive step sequences satisfy stochastic-approximation summability conditions, and the primal-dual iterates are almost surely bounded.

children.title: Lagrangian Stochastic Approximation
children.top_down_role: Constrained simulation optimization organized through stochastic Lagrangian information.

assumptions_latex: The convex program \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\leq0\) satisfies strong duality and has a dual solution.
For each multiplier, the inner stochastic recursion consistently approaches a minimizer of the Lagrangian over \(X\).
The outer multiplier steps satisfy stochastic-approximation summability conditions and evolve on a slower timescale than the inner recursion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stable limiting pairs minimize \(L(\cdot,\lambda^*)\) over \(X\) and maximize the dual function over \(\mathbb{R}_+^m\), hence solve the convex program.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \((x_0,\lambda_0)\in X\times\mathbb{R}_+^m\). Stop at the budget or a declared saddle-residual tolerance and output the final pair or specified averages.

assumptions_latex: Multiplier updates have the form \(\lambda_{k+1}=\Pi_{\mathbb{R}_+^m}(\lambda_k+b_k(\widehat g_k+r_k))\), with square-summable-noise steps and vanishing bias.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Multiplier stability is ensured by either of two regimes. In the projection regime, replace the orthant projection by projection onto a known compact convex set \(\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}_+^m\) containing a dual solution. In the drift regime, require a radially unbounded \(V:\mathbb{R}_+^m\to[0,\infty)\), a compact set \(K\), and \(c>0\) such that the conditional mean increment satisfies \[\mathbb{E}[V(\lambda_{k+1})-V(\lambda_k)\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq-cb_k\quad\text{whenever }\lambda_k\notin K,\] up to a summable error. Either condition prevents multiplier escape.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multipliers remain stable when explicitly projected onto a suitable compact set or when a radially unbounded Lyapunov function has negative drift outside a compact region.

children.title: Subgradient Stochastic Approximation
children.top_down_role: Recursive simulation optimization using noisy generalized direction information.

assumptions_latex: The function \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is proper, convex, and locally Lipschitz on a neighborhood containing the bounded iterates.
The observation satisfies \(G_k=s_k+M_{k+1}+r_k\), where \(s_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), the noise is a martingale difference with bounded conditional second moment, and \(r_k\to0\).
The steps satisfy \(a_k>0\), \(\sum_k a_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k a_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective values converge to \(f^*=\inf f\), and every accumulation point belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}f\) almost surely when the minimizer set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained convex stochastic subgradient recursion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At iteration \(k\), obtain a simulation-derived observation \(G_k\) of a subgradient and update \[x_{k+1}=x_k-a_kG_k.\] Stop at a prescribed simulation budget or a declared approximate-stationarity criterion, and return the last iterate or a specified weighted average. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take diminishing steps opposite noisy convex subgradients; bounded iterates with controlled noise approach the minimizer set almost surely.

children.title: Differential-Inclusion Regimes
children.top_down_role: Set-valued limiting dynamics arising from nonsmooth or discontinuous recursive behavior.

assumptions_latex: The set-valued drift \(H:\mathbb{R}^d\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^d\) is upper semicontinuous with nonempty compact convex values and at most linear growth.
The recursion is bounded and has martingale-difference noise with bounded conditional second moments, a vanishing perturbation, and standard stochastic-approximation steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interpolation is an asymptotic pseudo-trajectory of \(\dot x(t)\in H(x(t))\), and its limit set is an internally chain-transitive invariant set of that inclusion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ODE-method extension to compact convex set-valued drifts.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[x_{k+1}=x_k+a_k(v_k+M_{k+1}+r_k),\qquad v_k\in H(x_k).\] Define times \(t_0=0\), \(t_{k+1}=t_k+a_k\), and let \(\bar x(t)\) linearly interpolate \(x_k\) on \([t_k,t_{k+1}]\). Under the assumptions, every time-shifted subsequential limit of \(\bar x\) is an absolutely continuous solution of \[\dot x(t)\in H(x(t))\quad\text{for almost every }t.\] Thus the differential inclusion, rather than a single ordinary differential equation, represents the limiting dynamics when the mean field is nonsmooth or genuinely set-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded stochastic recursion with compact convex set-valued drift is asymptotically represented by the corresponding differential inclusion; its limit set is internally chain-transitive.

children.title: Set-Valued Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Stability limitations associated with nonunique directions or limiting trajectories.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Valued Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of boundedness without projection or inward Lyapunov drift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d=1\), let \(H(x)=\{x\}\), choose \(x_0>0\), and take noise and bias identically equal to zero. For any steps satisfying \(a_k>0\), \(a_k\to0\), and \(\sum_k a_k=\infty\), the recursion is \[x_{k+1}=x_k+a_kx_k=(1+a_k)x_k,\qquad x_k=x_0\prod_{j<k}(1+a_j),\] and satisfies \(x_k\to+\infty\). Thus a continuous, singleton-valued, convex-valued drift of linear growth does not ensure bounded stochastic-approximation iterates; an additional stability mechanism such as projection, coercivity, or negative Lyapunov drift outside a compact set is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With zero noise and drift H(x)={x}, every positive initial state diverges under diminishing positive steps whose sum is infinite. Regularity of the set-valued drift alone therefore does not ensure stability.
assumptions_latex: The steps satisfy \(a_k>0\), \(a_k\to0\), \(\sum_k a_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k a_k^2<\infty\).
No projection, coercive Lyapunov condition, or inward-drift condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Even a continuous singleton-valued drift with linear growth can produce unbounded iterates; regularity of the set-valued map alone does not establish stochastic-approximation stability.

children.title: Kiefer-Wolfowitz Family

children.title: Coordinate Kiefer-Wolfowitz Search
children.top_down_role: Coordinatewise finite-difference stochastic approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Kiefer-Wolfowitz Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical coordinatewise central-difference stochastic approximation for unconstrained smooth minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given noisy observations \(Y(x)=f(x)+\varepsilon\), initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At iteration \(k\), obtain independent observations \(Y_{k,i}^{\pm}\) at \(x_k\pm c_k e_i\) and form \[\widehat g_k=\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{Y_{k,i}^{+}-Y_{k,i}^{-}}{2c_k}e_i.\] Update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-a_k\widehat g_k\). Stop at a prescribed iteration or when a chosen stochastic stationarity diagnostic is met, and return the final iterate or an iterate average. Each iteration uses \(2d\) function measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate every gradient coordinate by two noisy symmetric function evaluations, then take a stochastic-approximation step; one iteration costs twice the dimension in measurements.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable near the iterates.
Observation errors have conditional mean zero and finite conditional variance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-a_k\widehat g_k\), using \(2d\) measurements per iteration.

children.title: Random-Direction Stochastic Approximation
children.top_down_role: Randomized directional approximations replacing coordinate sweeps.

knowledge_statements.title: Random-Direction Stochastic Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-measurement random-direction analogue of coordinate Kiefer-Wolfowitz search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). Independently draw a direction \(u_k\) satisfying \(\mathbb{E}[u_ku_k^{\mathsf T}]=I_d\), observe \(Y_k^{\pm}\) at \(x_k\pm c_ku_k\), and set \[\widehat g_k=\frac{Y_k^+-Y_k^-}{2c_k}u_k.\] Update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-a_k\widehat g_k\) and return the final or averaged iterate. For smooth \(f\), conditional expectation over the direction and centered observation noise gives \(\mathbb{E}[\widehat g_k\mid x_k]=\nabla f(x_k)+O(c_k^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random direction replaces the coordinate sweep, producing an approximately unbiased gradient estimate from two noisy evaluations regardless of dimension.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) has locally bounded third derivatives.
\(u_k\) is independent of the past, centered, and has sufficiently many finite moments.
Observation errors are conditionally centered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-a_k\widehat g_k\) with two measurements and \(\mathbb{E}[\widehat g_k\mid x_k]=\nabla f(x_k)+O(c_k^2)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Kiefer-Wolfowitz Convergence Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical strongly convex rate with central differences and independent bounded-variance noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose coordinate Kiefer-Wolfowitz search uses \(a_k=a/(k+1)\) and \(c_k=c(k+1)^{-1/6}\). If \(f\) is strongly convex with Lipschitz gradient, has uniformly bounded third coordinate derivatives, and the independent observation errors have uniformly bounded variance, then suitable positive constants \(a,c\) give \[\mathbb{E}\lVert x_k-x^\star\rVert^2=O(k^{-2/3}),\qquad \mathbb{E}[f(x_k)-f(x^\star)]=O(k^{-2/3}).\] Thus the root-mean-square iterate error is \(O(k^{-1/3})\); constants may depend on dimension and noise variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balancing central-difference bias against amplified independent noise yields mean-square iterate and objective-error rates of order two-thirds in the iteration count.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is strongly convex, smooth, and has bounded third coordinate derivatives.
Observation errors are independent, centered, and uniformly square-integrable.
The gain constants satisfy the usual stable stochastic-approximation range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}\lVert x_k-x^\star\rVert^2=O(k^{-2/3})\) and \(\mathbb{E}[f(x_k)-f(x^\star)]=O(k^{-2/3})\).

children.title: Kiefer-Wolfowitz Finite-Difference Bias
children.top_down_role: Approximation bias associated with finite-difference direction estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Kiefer-Wolfowitz Finite-Difference Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local truncation bias of the symmetric coordinate finite-difference estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For coordinate \(i\), define \(D_{i,c}f(x)=[f(x+ce_i)-f(x-ce_i)]/(2c)\). If the one-dimensional restriction \(t\mapsto f(x+te_i)\) is five times continuously differentiable near zero, then \[D_{i,c}f(x)=\partial_i f(x)+\frac{c^2}{6}\partial_{iii}f(x)+O(c^4).\] Consequently, centered observation noise does not change the conditional bias, and the coordinate Kiefer-Wolfowitz gradient estimator satisfies \(\mathbb{E}[\widehat g(x,c)]-\nabla f(x)=O(c^2)\) componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric coordinate difference has second-order bias; centered simulation noise changes its variance but not its conditional mean.
assumptions_latex: For every coordinate, \(t\mapsto f(x+te_i)\) is five times continuously differentiable near \(0\).
Noisy function observations have conditional mean \(f\) at each queried point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{i,c}f(x)-\partial_i f(x)=\frac{c^2}{6}\partial_{iii}f(x)+O(c^4)\), hence the estimator bias is \(O(c^2)\).

notation.meaning: symmetric finite difference in coordinate i

children.title: Noise-Dependence Rate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Rate behavior under independent, coupled, or serially dependent simulation noise.

knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Dependence Rate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias-variance regimes for averaged central differences under differently coupled simulation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Average \(n\) replicated central differences of radius \(c\), with deterministic bias \(O(c^2)\). If the paired observation-error difference satisfies \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon^+-\varepsilon^-)=O(c^{2q})\) for \(0\le q\le1\), then the gradient mean-square error is \[O(c^4)+O\!\left(n^{-1}c^{2q-2}\right).\] Balancing the terms gives \(c\asymp n^{-1/(6-2q)}\) and mean-square error \(O(n^{-4/(6-2q)})\). Independent noise corresponds to \(q=0\), giving \(O(n^{-2/3})\); sufficiently smooth common-random-number coupling corresponds to \(q=1\), giving \(O(n^{-1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stronger coupling of paired simulation noise reduces finite-difference variance and improves the optimally balanced gradient-estimation rate from two-thirds to the parametric rate.
assumptions_latex: The symmetric finite-difference bias is uniformly \(O(c^2)\).
Replicates are independent across pairs and have uniformly bounded second moments.
Within-pair noise obeys \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon^+-\varepsilon^-)=O(c^{2q})\) for some \(q\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The balanced gradient mean-square error is \(O(n^{-4/(6-2q)})\), ranging from \(O(n^{-2/3})\) to \(O(n^{-1})\).

children.title: Two-Measurement SPSA
children.top_down_role: Symmetric simultaneous-perturbation estimation.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Measurement SPSA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard first-order SPSA using one symmetric pair of simultaneous perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). At iteration \(k\), draw \(\Delta_k\) with independent symmetric nonzero components, observe \(Y_k^\pm\) at \(x_k\pm c_k\Delta_k\), and define \[\widehat g_{k,i}=\frac{Y_k^+-Y_k^-}{2c_k\Delta_{k,i}},\qquad i=1,\ldots,d.\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k-a_k\widehat g_k\). Stop at a prescribed budget or diagnostic and return the final or averaged iterate. The gradient estimate requires exactly two objective measurements per iteration, independently of dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two symmetric, simultaneously perturbed evaluations estimate every gradient component, so measurement cost per iteration does not grow with dimension.
assumptions_latex: Perturbation components are independent, symmetric, nonzero, and have finite inverse moments.
\(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is three times differentiable near the iterates.
Observation errors are conditionally centered with finite variance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-a_k\widehat g_k\), using exactly two measurements per iteration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-measurement SPSA formula and dimension-independent measurement count are standard and fit the algorithm leaf, but no inspectable source or locator is supplied.

children.title: One-Measurement SPSA
children.top_down_role: Reduced-evaluation simultaneous-perturbation estimation.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Measurement SPSA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-evaluation SPSA with cancellation supplied by symmetric perturbations rather than a baseline measurement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^d\). Draw a perturbation \(\Delta_k\) with independent symmetric nonzero components, take the single observation \(Y_k^+=Y(x_k+c_k\Delta_k)\), and set \[\widehat g_{k,i}=\frac{Y_k^+}{c_k\Delta_{k,i}},\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k-a_k\widehat g_k.\] Because \(\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{k,i}^{-1}]=0\), the common term \(f(x_k)/(c_k\Delta_{k,i})\) cancels in expectation, although it can cause substantially larger variance than the two-measurement estimator. Return the final or averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single perturbed evaluation can estimate the gradient through perturbation symmetry, but the uncancelled sample-level baseline usually increases variance.
assumptions_latex: Perturbation components are independent, symmetric, nonzero, and possess the required inverse moments.
\(f\) is differentiable with a locally controlled Taylor remainder.
The gain and perturbation sequences control the estimator's increasing variance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration uses one measurement, with \(\mathbb{E}[\widehat g_k\mid x_k]=\nabla f(x_k)+O(c_k)\) under the stated symmetry and smoothness conditions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this less-standard one-measurement variant. The conditional-mean conclusion also requires an explicit centered observation-noise assumption, and its stated bias order depends on the precise perturbation distribution and smoothness conditions.

children.title: Second-Order SPSA
children.top_down_role: Simultaneous perturbation with curvature estimation.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order SPSA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A simultaneous-perturbation Newton scheme using stochastic gradient and Hessian estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and a symmetric curvature estimate \(H_0\). At iteration \(k\), construct an SPSA gradient estimate \(\widehat g_k\) and an independent simultaneous-perturbation Hessian estimate \(\widehat H_k\) from noisy function measurements. Update \[H_{k+1}=H_k+b_k(\widehat H_k-H_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k-a_kR(H_{k+1})^{-1}\widehat g_k,\] where \(R\) maps a symmetric matrix to a uniformly positive-definite regularization. Stop at the simulation budget and return the final or averaged iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order SPSA recursively estimates curvature from simultaneous perturbations and applies a regularized stochastic Newton step.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is sufficiently smooth for consistent gradient and Hessian perturbation estimates.
Perturbations have symmetric nonzero components and sufficient inverse moments.
\(R(H)\) is uniformly positive definite and the gains satisfy stochastic-approximation conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k-a_kR(H_{k+1})^{-1}\widehat g_k\) uses the recursively smoothed curvature estimate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record describes the role of second-order SPSA but does not specify the simultaneous-perturbation Hessian estimator or measurement scheme. An authoritative variant-specific source is necessary before a complete algorithm statement can be assessed.

children.title: Adaptive SPSA
children.top_down_role: Online adaptation of scaling and perturbation behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive SPSA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A predictable-gain SPSA template whose scales adapt to accumulated simulation information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_k\) contain all observations through iteration \(k\). Before drawing \(\Delta_k\), choose positive \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable gains \(a_k,c_k\) from past gradients, objective values, or variance estimates. Form the two-measurement SPSA estimate \(\widehat g_k\) and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-a_k\widehat g_k\). Adaptation preserves the standard convergence mechanism when, almost surely, \[c_k\to0,\qquad \sum_k a_k=\infty,\qquad \sum_k\frac{a_k^2}{c_k^2}<\infty,\qquad \sum_k a_kc_k^2<\infty,\] together with boundedness or an appropriate stability condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SPSA scales may depend on past data while retaining convergence-compatible decay, noise summability, and finite accumulated finite-difference bias.
assumptions_latex: Adaptive gains are positive and measurable before the current perturbation and noise are sampled.
The SPSA noise has conditionally bounded variance after scaling.
Iterates are almost surely bounded or stabilized by projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Predictable adaptation is convergence-compatible when the displayed gain, variance, and bias summability conditions hold.

notation.meaning: information available before iteration k sampling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Adaptive SPSA denotes multiple schemes, and no source establishes that the displayed predictable-gain and summability conditions are sufficient for the claimed convergence compatibility in this formulation.

children.title: Constrained SPSA

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained SPSA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected first-order SPSA for a closed convex feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and initialize \(x_0\in C\). Construct a simultaneous-perturbation estimate \(\widehat g_k\), using feasible simulation queries or an extension of the objective outside \(C\), and update \[x_{k+1}=\Pi_C(x_k-a_k\widehat g_k),\qquad \Pi_C(z)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}\lVert y-z\rVert.\] Stop at a prescribed budget and return the final or averaged feasible iterate. Projection guarantees \(x_k\in C\) but does not by itself make infeasible perturbation queries valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection after each SPSA step preserves feasibility, provided perturbed objective evaluations are themselves well-defined or replaced by feasible queries.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The objective oracle is defined at perturbation points or a specified feasible perturbation rule is used.
Step sizes and estimator noise satisfy the applicable projected stochastic-approximation conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_C(x_k-a_k\widehat g_k)\in C\) for every \(k\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the feasible region

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projected update correctly preserves feasibility and appropriately flags the perturbation-query issue, but no locator supports the selected constrained-SPSA formulation or its boundary handling.

children.title: Discrete SPSA
children.top_down_role: SPSA variants adapted to discrete or quantized decision spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete SPSA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A projected latent-space SPSA heuristic for finite or integer-valued decision sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\) be finite and let \(P_D:\mathbb{R}^d\to D\) be a fixed rounding or nearest-point map. Maintain a latent state \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^d\), query \(z_k^\pm=P_D(x_k\pm c_k\Delta_k)\), and, when \(z_k^+\ne z_k^-\), form a specified finite-difference estimate \(\widehat g_k\) from \(Y(z_k^+)\) and \(Y(z_k^-)\). Update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-a_k\widehat g_k\) and retain the best statistically validated point in \(D\). If both projections coincide, resample or enlarge \(c_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous latent SPSA step is mapped to discrete feasible queries; coincident rounded perturbations must be detected because they contain no difference information.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\) is finite and the projection rule \(P_D\) is fixed.
Simulation observations are available at every queried point of \(D\).
Incumbent comparisons use a prescribed replication or statistical-selection rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every evaluated and returned decision lies in \(D\); coincident projected perturbations trigger resampling or radius enlargement.

notation.meaning: rounding or projection map into the discrete set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Discrete SPSA is not a unique algorithm, and this record leaves the finite-difference estimator and incumbent-validation rule unspecified. A variant-specific authoritative source is required.

children.title: Global SPSA
children.top_down_role: SPSA variants incorporating mechanisms intended to move beyond purely local search.

knowledge_statements.title: Global SPSA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A restart-based SPSA construction with global coverage and statistically consistent incumbent selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be compact. For restart \(r\), sample \(X_r\) independently from a distribution assigning positive probability to every nonempty relatively open subset of \(C\), run a finite constrained SPSA trajectory from \(X_r\), and add both its start and visited points to the candidate set. Reestimate candidate objectives with increasing replication and retain the smallest consistent estimate. If \(f\) is continuous and the retained estimates are uniformly consistent over accumulated candidates, then the incumbent objective converges almost surely to \(\min_{x\in C}f(x)\) as the number of restarts tends to infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-support random restarts provide global coverage, while local SPSA refines candidates and increasing replication prevents persistent selection by noise.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is compact and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous.
Restart points are independent and have full support on \(C\).
Incumbent objective estimates become uniformly consistent over the accumulated finite candidate sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\widehat x_R\) is the incumbent after \(R\) restarts, then \(f(\widehat x_R)\to\min_{x\in C}f(x)\) almost surely.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restart construction is plausible, but Global SPSA has no single standard formulation. The almost-sure global convergence conclusion and the required meaning and attainability of uniform consistency over a growing candidate collection need direct theorem-level support.

children.title: SPSA Gain Regimes
children.top_down_role: Families of adaptation-scale behavior governing responsiveness and stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: SPSA Gain Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard diminishing-gain conditions for first-order SPSA recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the SPSA recursion use positive gains \(a_k\). The classical diminishing-gain regime is characterized by \[a_k\to0,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k=\infty,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k^2<\infty.\] Thus adaptation persists indefinitely while square-summable gains control stochastic fluctuations of bounded-variance gradient estimates. For the power family \(a_k=a(k+A)^{-\alpha}\), where \(a>0\) and \(A\ge0\), these gain-only conditions hold whenever \(1/2<\alpha\le1\). Because SPSA gradient-estimate variance generally grows as perturbations vanish, convergence additionally requires gain-to-perturbation coupling conditions stated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive SPSA gains should vanish, have divergent sum, and be square summable; power gains satisfy this when their exponent lies between one-half and one.
assumptions_latex: a_k>0\ \text{for every }k
a>0,\ A\ge 0\ \text{in the power-law parameterization}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_k\to0,\quad \sum_k a_k=\infty,\quad \sum_k a_k^2<\infty

notation.meaning: SPSA update gain at iteration k

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports SPSA gain conditions.
REQUEST_SOURCES: authoritative SPSA convergence theorem or monograph section required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, but no inspectable SPSA convergence citation is supplied. Also, with indexing from k=0, the parameterization a_k=a(k+A)^{-\alpha} is not defined when A=0; require A>0 or use k+1.

children.title: SPSA Perturbation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Families of perturbation-scale behavior governing directional information quality.

knowledge_statements.title: SPSA Perturbation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing deterministic magnitudes and admissible random perturbation vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(c_k>0\) be the perturbation magnitude and let \(\Delta_k\in\mathbb R^p\) have independent, symmetric components. A standard SPSA perturbation regime requires \[c_k\to0,\qquad \mathbb E[\Delta_{ki}]=0,\qquad \mathbb E[\Delta_{ki}^{-2}]<\infty,\] with the inverse second moments uniformly bounded in \(k\) and \(i\). The power regime \(c_k=c(k+1)^{-\gamma}\), with \(c>0\) and \(\gamma>0\), satisfies the magnitude condition. Rademacher components, taking values \(\pm1\) equiprobably, satisfy the component conditions and avoid perturbations arbitrarily close to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SPSA uses perturbation magnitudes tending to zero and symmetric random directions whose reciprocal components have uniformly finite second moments.
assumptions_latex: c_k>0
\Delta_k\ \text{is independent of the past at iteration }k
\Delta_{ki}\ne0\ \text{almost surely}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c_k\to0\ \text{and}\ \sup_{k,i}\mathbb E[\Delta_{ki}^{-2}]<\infty
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports SPSA perturbation assumptions.
REQUEST_SOURCES: primary SPSA convergence source required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role and local scope are appropriate, but the exact perturbation assumptions, including component independence, symmetry, inverse moments, and independence from the past, require a specifically located SPSA source.

children.title: Gain-to-Perturbation Coupling
children.top_down_role: Joint scale relationships affecting the balance between adaptation and gradient-estimation quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Gain-to-Perturbation Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient summability coupling for central-difference SPSA with smooth responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the conditional bias of the two-sided SPSA gradient estimator is \(O(c_k^2)\), while its conditional noise variance is \(O(c_k^{-2})\). A sufficient coupling for almost-sure stochastic-approximation convergence is \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k=\infty,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{a_k^2}{c_k^2}<\infty,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_kc_k^2<\infty.\] For \(a_k=a(k+A)^{-\alpha}\) and \(c_k=c(k+1)^{-\gamma}\), these conditions reduce to \(\alpha\le1\), \(2\alpha-2\gamma>1\), and \(\alpha+2\gamma>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gains must dominate neither amplified observation noise nor finite-difference bias; power exponents obey three corresponding inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \|\mathbb E[\widehat g_k-\nabla f(x_k)\mid\mathcal F_k]\|=O(c_k^2)
\mathbb E[\|\widehat g_k-\mathbb E[\widehat g_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=O(c_k^{-2})
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_k a_k^2c_k^{-2}<\infty\quad\text{and}\quad\sum_k a_kc_k^2<\infty

notation.meaning: information available before iteration k observations

review_flags: Exact SPSA summability theorem is unsupported by supplied locators.
The bias-summability requirement is sufficient and may be stronger than some convergence theorems.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits the coupling leaf and the exponent algebra is consistent, but the asserted almost-sure sufficiency and the bias summability requirement need verification against a specifically located convergence theorem.

children.title: SPSA Noise-Regularity Regime Family

children.title: SPSA Noise Regimes
children.top_down_role: Simulation-noise families relevant to SPSA behavior, including dependence and heterogeneity.

knowledge_statements.title: SPSA Noise Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Martingale-difference observation noise with variance amplified by finite differencing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the two observations as \(Y_k^{\pm}=f(x_k\pm c_k\Delta_k)+\varepsilon_k^{\pm}\), and define \(\eta_k=\varepsilon_k^+-\varepsilon_k^-\). In the standard noise regime, \[\mathbb E[\eta_k\mid\mathcal F_k,\Delta_k]=0,\qquad \mathbb E[\eta_k^2\mid\mathcal F_k,\Delta_k]\le \sigma^2\] almost surely for a finite \(\sigma^2\). If the reciprocal perturbation moments are uniformly bounded, the noise component of each SPSA gradient estimate has conditional second moment \(O(c_k^{-2})\). Consequently, the weighted noise series is controlled by the sufficient condition \(\sum_k a_k^2/c_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditionally unbiased paired observation noise with bounded variance becomes order inverse-perturbation-squared gradient noise, requiring compatible gains.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb E[\eta_k\mid\mathcal F_k,\Delta_k]=0
\mathbb E[\eta_k^2\mid\mathcal F_k,\Delta_k]\le\sigma^2<\infty
\sup_{k,i}\mathbb E[\Delta_{ki}^{-2}]<\infty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[\|\widehat g_k-\mathbb E[\widehat g_k\mid\mathcal F_k,\Delta_k]\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=O(c_k^{-2})
review_flags: Supplied sources do not locate the SPSA martingale-noise theorem.
REQUEST_SOURCES: source distinguishing observation-noise and gradient-noise assumptions required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits, but no source supports the stated SPSA noise regime. The conclusion conditions only on F_k while centering by an expectation conditional on both F_k and Delta_k, and the unconditional reciprocal-moment assumption does not directly give a deterministic bound after conditioning on Delta_k; the precise formulation requires source verification.

children.title: SPSA Response-Regularity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Smoothness and local response structures supporting SPSA analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: SPSA Response-Regularity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias orders for two-sided SPSA under alternative smoothness assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\), and form the two-sided SPSA estimator from \(f(x+c\Delta)\) and \(f(x-c\Delta)\). On a neighborhood of \(x\), bounded third derivatives give \[\mathbb E[\widehat g(x,c,\Delta)]-\nabla f(x)=O(c^2).\] If instead \(f\) is differentiable with locally Lipschitz gradient, the central quotient remains consistent but only the bound \(O(c)\) follows without stronger regularity. Mere local Lipschitz continuity of \(f\) does not define a classical gradient and therefore does not, by itself, ensure convergence of the estimator to \(\nabla f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Third-order smoothness yields quadratic SPSA bias; Lipschitz gradients yield a weaker bound, while nonsmooth responses need a different target.
assumptions_latex: \Delta\ \text{has symmetric independent components and bounded inverse moments}
x\pm c\Delta\ \text{remain in the stated regularity neighborhood}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\in C^3\Rightarrow \mathbb E[\widehat g]-\nabla f(x)=O(c^2)
review_flags: Exact regularity-to-bias orders need a supporting SPSA Taylor-expansion source.
The Lipschitz-gradient order is a conservative sufficient bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits the regularity leaf, but bounded inverse moments alone do not control the positive perturbation moments used in a third-order Taylor remainder. The O(c^2) and O(c) bias claims need a source and a complete perturbation-moment hypothesis.

children.title: SPSA Dependence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Temporal or cross-perturbation dependence structures affecting SPSA estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: SPSA Dependence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified conditional-bias and variance conditions covering dependent simulation observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the centered error in the SPSA gradient estimate be \(M_{k+1}\), and let its predictable conditional bias be \(b_k\). Independence across iterations is unnecessary if \[\mathbb E[M_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]=0,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k^2\mathbb E[\|M_{k+1}\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]<\infty,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k\|b_k\|<\infty\] almost surely. Thus martingale-difference noise is directly admissible. Markov or mixing simulation output is admissible only when its gradient-error decomposition satisfies the same summable conditional-bias and conditional-variance bounds, possibly after batching or regeneration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent SPSA observations are admissible when their gradient errors decompose into controlled martingale noise and summable predictable bias.
assumptions_latex: M_{k+1}\ \text{is adapted to }\mathcal F_{k+1}
a_k>0
b_k=\mathbb E[\widehat g_k\mid\mathcal F_k]-\nabla f(x_k)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_k a_kM_{k+1}\ \text{converges almost surely and}\ \sum_k a_k\|b_k\|<\infty

notation.meaning: simulation and iterate history through iteration k

review_flags: A source for SPSA with Markov or mixing observations is required.
Statement gives sufficient decomposition conditions, not a characterization of every dependence regime.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role is appropriate, but the extension to Markov or mixing simulation output is nontrivial and has no inspectable citation. A source must specify the decomposition and conditions under which batching or regeneration yields the asserted summability bounds.

children.title: SPSA Irregular-Response Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Response pathologies that undermine standard SPSA analytical regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: SPSA Irregular-Response Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discontinuity can make the symmetric SPSA quotient diverge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In one dimension, take the noise-free response \(f(x)=\mathbf 1_{\{x\ge0\}}\), evaluate at \(x=0\), and use the deterministic perturbation \(\Delta=1\). The symmetric SPSA estimate is \[\widehat g(0,c,1)=\frac{f(c)-f(-c)}{2c}=\frac{1}{2c}.\] Hence \(\widehat g(0,c,1)\to+\infty\) as \(c\downarrow0\). The response has no classical derivative at the evaluation point, and shrinking perturbations do not produce a finite gradient surrogate. Smooth-response SPSA convergence results therefore cannot be extended to discontinuous objectives without changing the estimator, target generalized derivative, or smoothing model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a step response, the symmetric SPSA quotient diverges as perturbations vanish, so smooth-response convergence theory no longer applies.
assumptions_latex: f(x)=\mathbf 1_{\{x\ge0\}}
\Delta=1,\ c>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat g(0,c,1)=\frac{1}{2c}\to+\infty\quad\text{as }c\downarrow0
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct elementary counterexample; no external citation needed for candidate status.
Source certification remains desirable for the broader failure interpretation.

children.title: SPSA Asymptotic Performance Results

children.title: SPSA Almost-Sure Limits
children.top_down_role: Long-run pathwise behavior of SPSA iterates across supported regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: SPSA Almost-Sure Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure convergence to a unique stable stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x_{k+1}=x_k-a_k\widehat g_k\) on a compact invariant set. Suppose \(f\) is continuously differentiable, \(\widehat g_k=\nabla f(x_k)+b_k+M_{k+1}\), \(\sum_k a_k\|b_k\|<\infty\) almost surely, and \(M_{k+1}\) is a martingale difference satisfying \(\sum_k a_k^2\mathbb E[\|M_{k+1}\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]<\infty\). If \(a_k\to0\), \(\sum_k a_k=\infty\), and the differential equation \(\dot x=-\nabla f(x)\) has a unique globally asymptotically stable equilibrium \(x^*\) on that set, then \[x_k\to x^*\qquad\text{almost surely}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under stability, summable bias, controlled martingale noise, and persistent diminishing gains, SPSA converges almost surely to the unique stable equilibrium.
assumptions_latex: \{x_k\}\ \text{remains in a compact invariant set}
\sum_k a_k\|b_k\|<\infty\ \text{and}\ \sum_k a_k^2\mathbb E[\|M_{k+1}\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]<\infty
x^*\ \text{is the unique globally asymptotically stable equilibrium of }\dot x=-\nabla f(x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\to x^*\quad\text{almost surely}
review_flags: No supplied locator identifies an SPSA almost-sure convergence theorem.
Projection and local-attractor variants are intentionally excluded.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the almost-sure-limit leaf, but no theorem locator is supplied. Continuous differentiability alone does not ensure uniqueness of solutions for the gradient ODE, and the stated compact invariance and martingale conditions must be checked against a precise stochastic-approximation convergence theorem.

children.title: SPSA Asymptotic Distributions
children.top_down_role: Large-sample distributional behavior of scaled SPSA estimation error.

knowledge_statements.title: SPSA Asymptotic Distributions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central limit regime for power perturbations and harmonic gains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_k=a/k\), \(c_k=c/k^\gamma\), and \(\beta=1/2-\gamma\), where \(1/6<\gamma<1/2\). Suppose \(x_k\to x^*\), \(H=\nabla^2f(x^*)\) is positive definite, the scaled gradient noise has limiting covariance \(S\), and higher conditional moments satisfy a martingale central limit condition. If every eigenvalue of \(aH\) exceeds \(\beta\), then \[k^\beta(x_k-x^*)\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma),\] where \(\Sigma\) is the unique solution of \[(aH-\beta I)\Sigma+\Sigma(aH-\beta I)^{\mathsf T}=\frac{a^2}{c^2}S.\] At \(\gamma=1/6\), the same scaling can acquire a nonzero mean from the leading finite-difference bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With harmonic gains and power perturbations, suitably scaled SPSA errors converge to a Gaussian law whose covariance solves a Lyapunov equation.
assumptions_latex: x_k\to x^*\ \text{and}\ H=\nabla^2f(x^*)\succ0
1/6<\gamma<1/2\ \text{and}\ \lambda_{\min}(aH)>1/2-\gamma
\text{scaled martingale noise obeys a conditional central limit theorem with covariance }S
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k^{1/2-\gamma}(x_k-x^*)\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma)

notation.meaning: objective Hessian at the limiting point
limiting covariance of scaled gradient noise

review_flags: Exact normalization and Lyapunov covariance require verification against a primary SPSA asymptotic-normality theorem.
Boundary mean at gamma equals one-sixth depends on third-order bias constants.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role is correct for this leaf, but the normalization, stability threshold, covariance convention for S, Lyapunov equation, and boundary mean at gamma=1/6 are source-sensitive and cannot be certified without a specifically located primary asymptotic-normality result.

children.title: SPSA Comparative Efficiency
children.top_down_role: Performance comparisons between SPSA and alternative direction-estimation families.

knowledge_statements.title: SPSA Comparative Efficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration simulation cost relative to coordinate finite differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a parameter vector in \(\mathbb R^p\), a two-sided SPSA gradient estimate uses the paired responses \(Y(x+c\Delta)\) and \(Y(x-c\Delta)\); hence it requires exactly two response evaluations per iteration, independently of \(p\). A two-sided coordinate finite-difference gradient uses \(Y(x+ce_i)\) and \(Y(x-ce_i)\) for every coordinate and therefore requires \(2p\) evaluations. Thus, for equal iteration counts, SPSA reduces the response-evaluation ratio to \[\frac{2}{2p}=\frac1p.\] This is a simulation-cost comparison only; it does not assert equal estimator variance, iteration complexity, or asymptotic covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-sided SPSA uses two simulations per gradient estimate, versus twice the dimension for coordinate finite differences; statistical efficiency is separate.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb R^p
\text{both methods use two-sided response differences}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{SPSA}}=2,\qquad N_{\mathrm{CFD}}=2p,\qquad N_{\mathrm{SPSA}}/N_{\mathrm{CFD}}=1/p
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: evaluation counts follow directly from the two estimator definitions.

children.title: Decreasing-Gain Regime
children.top_down_role: Vanishing adaptation used for asymptotic convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Decreasing-Gain Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robbins–Monro step-size regime for asymptotic stochastic approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stochastic-approximation recursion \(x_{k+1}=x_k+a_kH_k\) is in the decreasing-gain regime when its deterministic gains satisfy \[a_k>0,\qquad a_k\to0,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k=\infty,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k^2<\infty.\] The divergent first sum provides unbounded algorithmic time, while square summability limits accumulated martingale noise having uniformly bounded conditional second moments. For the power family \(a_k=a(k+A)^{-\alpha}\), with \(a>0\) and \(A\ge0\), the regime holds exactly when \(1/2<\alpha\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decreasing gains vanish, sum to infinity, and have finite squared sum; power-law gains qualify for exponents above one-half through one.
assumptions_latex: a_k\ \text{is deterministic and positive}
a>0,\ A\ge0\ \text{for the power family}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_k\to0,\quad \sum_k a_k=\infty,\quad \sum_k a_k^2<\infty
review_flags: Supplied Kushner–Yin locator does not identify the step-size assumptions precisely.
REQUEST_SOURCES: exact stochastic-approximation assumptions section or theorem required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the decreasing-gain leaf, but the exact stochastic-approximation regime lacks a specific source locator. In addition, with k starting at zero, a_k=a(k+A)^{-\alpha} is undefined for A=0; require A>0 or replace k+A by k+1+A.

children.title: Constant-Gain Regime
children.top_down_role: Persistent adaptation used for tracking and steady-state error analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Gain Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed positive step size for persistent stochastic-approximation adaptation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the recursion \(X_{n+1}=X_n+\alpha(h(X_n)+M_{n+1})\), where \(\alpha>0\) is independent of \(n\). Its gain sequence satisfies \(\sum_n\alpha=\sum_n\alpha^2=\infty\), so it does not meet the classical square-summable decreasing-gain condition. Consequently, persistent observation noise is not asymptotically suppressed; under stability and suitable ergodicity assumptions, performance is described by an invariant distribution concentrated near the attracting set as \(\alpha\downarrow0\), rather than by almost-sure convergence for fixed \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed gain permits continual tracking but does not eliminate persistent noise; stable iterates generally fluctuate around an attractor with a gain-dependent steady-state error.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha>0\) is constant.
\((M_{n+1})\) is persistent stochastic noise.
The constant-gain recursion is stable and admits an invariant law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For fixed \(\alpha\), the iterates generally have nonzero steady-state dispersion rather than classical decreasing-gain almost-sure convergence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the Constant-Gain Regime container, and the fixed-gain summability observation is correct. However, the invariant-law concentration and steady-state claims require precise stability, recurrence, and ergodicity hypotheses plus a specific authoritative locator. The absence of any citation makes the mathematical scope unreliable.

children.title: Random Gain Sequences
children.top_down_role: Gain schedules whose magnitudes or timing contain stochastic variation.

knowledge_statements.title: Random Gain Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictable stochastic gains preserving martingale-noise cancellation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_n)\) be a filtration and let \(A_n\) be a nonnegative, \(\mathcal F_n\)-measurable gain used in \(X_{n+1}=X_n+A_n(h(X_n)+M_{n+1})\). A pathwise Robbins--Monro random-gain condition is \[\mathbb P\!\left(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}A_n=\infty,\quad \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}A_n^2<\infty\right)=1.\] If \(\mathbb E[M_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]=0\), predictability of \(A_n\) gives \(\mathbb E[A_nM_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]=0\); thus the gain-weighted noise remains a martingale difference with finite accumulated conditional variance when the corresponding second moments are bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random gains are admissible when they are predictable, have infinite total mass, and have finite squared mass almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \(A_n\geq0\) is \(\mathcal F_n\)-measurable.
\(\mathbb E[M_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]=0\).
Conditional noise second moments are uniformly bounded or suitably growth-controlled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weighted noise \((A_nM_{n+1})\) remains centered and has square-summable conditional variance.

notation.meaning: information available before the next observation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is the appropriate content kind, but no source supports the random-gain version. The state and noise spaces are not specified, and the conclusion about finite accumulated conditional variance needs an explicit almost-sure bound that is compatible with the random gains.

children.title: Two-Time-Scale Gains
children.top_down_role: Paired gain schedules operating at asymptotically separated speeds.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Time-Scale Gains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separated stochastic-approximation gains for coupled fast and slow recursions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For coupled recursions with gains \((a_n)\) and \((b_n)\), the standard two-time-scale condition is \[a_n>0,\quad b_n>0,\quad \sum_na_n=\sum_nb_n=\infty,\quad \sum_n(a_n^2+b_n^2)<\infty,\quad \frac{b_n}{a_n}\longrightarrow0.\] On the time scale generated by \((a_n)\), the variable updated with gain \(b_n\) is asymptotically frozen. On the time scale generated by \((b_n)\), the variable updated with gain \(a_n\) is treated through its fast limiting equilibrium or invariant set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both gains satisfy stochastic-approximation summability, while the slow gain is asymptotically negligible relative to the fast gain.
assumptions_latex: \((a_n)\) and \((b_n)\) are positive deterministic or predictable sequences.
Both gain sequences have infinite mass and finite squared mass.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The \(a_n\)-recursion is fast and the \(b_n\)-recursion is slow.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed gain conditions and scale convention are standard and fit this leaf as a condition. Nevertheless, the coupled variables and recursions are not introduced, and no cited source establishes the precise deterministic-or-predictable formulation or the limiting-equilibrium interpretation.

children.title: Cross-Scale Coupling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Interaction patterns between fast-recursion behavior and slow-recursion evolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Scale Coupling Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of coupled gain scales by their asymptotic ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((a_n)\) and \((b_n)\) be positive gains for two coupled stochastic recursions, and suppose the extended limit \(\lambda=\lim_{n\to\infty}b_n/a_n\in[0,\infty]\) exists. The regime is fast--slow with the \(a_n\)-component fast when \(\lambda=0\); jointly coupled when \(0<\lambda<\infty\), in which case both drifts enter one common limiting time scale with relative weight \(\lambda\); and fast--slow with the \(b_n\)-component fast when \(\lambda=\infty\). If the ratio has no limit, subsequential ratios can induce multiple limiting coupling regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gain ratio determines whether one recursion is asymptotically faster or whether both remain coupled on a common time scale.
assumptions_latex: The ratio \(b_n/a_n\) has an extended limit for the three-regime classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limit \(\lambda\in\{0\}\cup(0,\infty)\cup\{\infty\}\) determines the asymptotic cross-scale coupling regime.

notation.meaning: gains of the two coupled recursions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is suitable for this classification leaf, but the common-time-scale claim refers to drifts that are never introduced. The ratio convention and the assertion about multiple subsequential limiting regimes also require a specific source locator.

children.title: Noise-Dependence Regimes

children.title: Martingale-Difference Noise
children.top_down_role: Classical centered-noise convergence regime.

assumptions_latex: \((X_n)\) is an \(\mathbb R^d\)-valued process adapted to \((\mathcal F_n)\).
\(M_{n+1}\in\mathbb R^d\) is \(\mathcal F_{n+1}\)-measurable and square-integrable, with \(\mathbb E[M_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]=0\).
\(a_n\geq0\) is \(\mathcal F_n\)-measurable, \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_n^2<\infty\) almost surely, and \(\mathbb E[\lVert M_{n+1}\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_n]\leq C(1+\lVert X_n\rVert^2)\).
The iterates satisfy \(\sup_n\lVert X_n\rVert<\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The series \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_nM_{n+1}\) converges almost surely in \(\mathbb R^d\).

notation.meaning: martingale-difference noise observed after iteration n

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F_n)_{n\geq0}\) be a filtration, let \((X_n)_{n\geq0}\) be an adapted \(\mathbb R^d\)-valued process, and let \(M_{n+1}\in\mathbb R^d\) be \(\mathcal F_{n+1}\)-measurable and square-integrable. The sequence is martingale-difference noise when \[\mathbb E[M_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]=0\quad\text{almost surely for every }n\geq0.\] Suppose also that \[\mathbb E[\lVert M_{n+1}\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_n]\leq C(1+\lVert X_n\rVert^2)\] for a deterministic constant \(C<\infty\). If \(a_n\geq0\) is \(\mathcal F_n\)-measurable, \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_n^2<\infty\) almost surely, and \(\sup_n\lVert X_n\rVert<\infty\) almost surely, then the martingale series \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_nM_{n+1}\) converges almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Martingale-difference noise has zero conditional mean given the past. Under the stated conditional second-moment bound, predictable square-summable gains and almost-surely bounded iterates make the accumulated weighted noise converge almost surely.
knowledge_statements.title: Martingale-Difference Noise

children.title: Correlated Noise
children.top_down_role: Recursive search with temporally dependent observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Correlated Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Poisson-equation decomposition for temporally dependent Markov observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((Z_n)\) be a Markov process with transition kernel \(P_x\) when the iterate is frozen at \(x\), invariant law \(\pi_x\), and observation \(g(x,Z_{n+1})\). Define \(\bar g(x)=\int g(x,z)\,\pi_x(dz)\). If the Poisson equation \[u_x-P_xu_x=g(x,\cdot)-\bar g(x)\] has a suitably integrable solution, then the centered observation admits a martingale-increment plus telescoping-remainder decomposition. Under regularity of \(P_x,u_x\), slowly varying iterates, and decreasing gains, the weighted remainder is asymptotically negligible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Markov-correlated observations can be separated into a martingale increment and a negligible telescoping remainder by solving a Poisson equation.
assumptions_latex: For each frozen \(x\), \(P_x\) admits invariant law \(\pi_x\).
The displayed Poisson equation has a suitably integrable solution \(u_x\).
Iterates and kernels vary slowly enough to control the remainder.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The centered correlated noise has a martingale-plus-remainder representation suitable for stochastic-approximation analysis.

notation.meaning: invariant law of the frozen kernel

children.title: State-Dependent Noise
children.top_down_role: Noise laws coupled to current decisions or simulated states.

assumptions_latex: \((\mathsf Z,\mathcal Z)\) is a measurable observation space and \(Q\) is a Markov kernel from \(\mathbb R^d\) to \((\mathsf Z,\mathcal Z)\).
\(X_n\in\mathbb R^d\) is \(\mathcal F_n\)-measurable and the conditional law of \(Z_{n+1}\) given \(\mathcal F_n\) is \(Q(X_n,\cdot)\).
\(H:\mathbb R^d\times\mathsf Z\to\mathbb R^d\) is measurable and \(H(X_n,Z_{n+1})\) is conditionally integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual \(M_{n+1}\) is conditionally centered, while its conditional distribution and moments may depend on \(X_n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noise whose conditional distribution depends on the current finite-dimensional iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathsf Z,\mathcal Z)\) be a measurable space, let \(Q\) be a Markov kernel from \(\mathbb R^d\) to \((\mathsf Z,\mathcal Z)\), and let \(X_n\in\mathbb R^d\) be \(\mathcal F_n\)-measurable. Suppose that, conditionally on \(\mathcal F_n\), the random variable \(Z_{n+1}\in\mathsf Z\) has law \(Q(X_n,\cdot)\). For a measurable, conditionally integrable map \(H:\mathbb R^d\times\mathsf Z\to\mathbb R^d\), define \[h(x)=\int_{\mathsf Z}H(x,z)Q(x,dz),\qquad M_{n+1}=H(X_n,Z_{n+1})-h(X_n).\] Then \(\mathbb E[M_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]=0\) almost surely. The residual is state-dependent because its conditional distribution, and generally its conditional moments, depend on \(X_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The current iterate selects the conditional law of the next observation. Subtracting the mean under that state-specific law produces a conditionally centered residual whose distribution and moments may still depend on the iterate.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Dependent Noise

children.title: Projected ODE Limits

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(h:C\to\mathbb R^d\) is a drift field for which the projected differential equation is well posed.
\(a_n>0\), \(X_n\in C\), and \(M_{n+1}\in\mathbb R^d\) in the displayed projected recursion.

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone of C at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal projected limiting flow for a stochastic-approximation recursion constrained to a closed convex set.

source_refs.source_title: Stochastic Approximation and Recursive Algorithms and Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(\Pi_C:\mathbb R^d\to C\) be the Euclidean projection. For \(x\in C\) and \(v\in\mathbb R^d\), define \[\pi_C(x,v)=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\frac{\Pi_C(x+\delta v)-x}{\delta}.\] For a drift \(h:C\to\mathbb R^d\), the formal limiting flow associated with the projected recursion \[X_{n+1}=\Pi_C\bigl(X_n+a_n(h(X_n)+M_{n+1})\bigr),\qquad X_n\in C,\quad a_n>0,\quad M_{n+1}\in\mathbb R^d,\] is \[\dot x(t)=\pi_C(x(t),h(x(t))),\qquad x(t)\in C.\] For closed convex \(C\), \(\pi_C(x,h(x))\) equals the Euclidean projection of \(h(x)\) onto the tangent cone \(T_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a recursion projected onto a closed convex set, the associated limiting velocity is obtained by projecting the drift onto the feasible tangent cone. This record identifies the limiting equation but does not itself assert convergence of an interpolation to that equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected ODE Limits

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space, let \(\Phi:[0,\infty)\times X\to X\) be a continuous semiflow, and let \(x:[0,\infty)\to X\) be a continuous asymptotic pseudo-trajectory of \(\Phi\) whose range has compact closure. Then its omega-limit set \(L(x)\) is nonempty, compact, connected, invariant, and internally chain transitive. In particular, every point of \(L(x)\) is chain recurrent for the semiflow restricted to \(L(x)\). Thus a precompact stochastic-approximation interpolation satisfying the ODE-method tracking property can have a limit set larger than the equilibrium set, but its limit set has this chain-recurrence structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A precompact trajectory that asymptotically tracks a continuous semiflow has a nonempty compact, connected, invariant, internally chain-transitive limit set consisting of chain-recurrent points.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An \(\mathbb R^d\)-valued recursion \((X_n)_{n\geq0}\) is almost surely stable when \[\mathbb P\!\left(\sup_{n\geq0}\lVert X_n\rVert<\infty\right)=1.\] A weaker uniform marginal tightness condition is that for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists a compact set \(K_\varepsilon\subset\mathbb R^d\) such that \[\sup_{n\geq0}\mathbb P(X_n\notin K_\varepsilon)\leq\varepsilon.\] Almost-sure stability yields pathwise precompactness in finite dimensions. Uniform marginal tightness alone does not imply that an entire sample path is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Almost-sure stability means that each full sample path is bounded. Uniform control of the one-time marginal distributions is weaker and does not by itself keep an entire path in a bounded set.

assumptions_latex: \((X_n)\) is adapted to \((\mathcal F_n)\), and \(V(X_n)\) is nonnegative and integrable for every \(n\).
\(V:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)\) is coercive and \(W:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)\) is measurable.
\((a_n)\) and \((b_n)\) are deterministic nonnegative sequences, \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}b_n<\infty\), and the displayed conditional-drift inequality holds.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X_n)_{n\geq0}\) be adapted to a filtration \((\mathcal F_n)_{n\geq0}\). Let \(V:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)\) be coercive, with \(V(X_n)\) integrable for every \(n\), and let \(W:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)\) be measurable. Suppose that deterministic sequences \((a_n)\) and \((b_n)\) satisfy \(a_n,b_n\geq0\), \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}b_n<\infty\), and \[\mathbb E[V(X_{n+1})\mid\mathcal F_n]\leq V(X_n)-a_nW(X_n)+b_n\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Then \(V(X_n)\) converges to a finite random variable almost surely and \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_nW(X_n)<\infty\) almost surely. Consequently, \(\sup_nV(X_n)<\infty\) almost surely; coercivity of \(V\) then yields \(\sup_n\lVert X_n\rVert<\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For integrable adapted iterates, a coercive nonnegative Lyapunov function whose conditional drift is negative up to deterministic summable errors gives finite accumulated dissipation and almost-sure boundedness.
knowledge_statements.title: Lyapunov Drift Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Containment via Rescaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ODE-at-infinity criterion for bounded stochastic-approximation iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(X_{n+1}=X_n+a_n(h(X_n)+M_{n+1})\) with globally Lipschitz \(h\). For \(c\geq1\), set \(h_c(x)=h(cx)/c\), and suppose \(h_c\to h_\infty\) uniformly on compact sets as \(c\to\infty\). If the origin is a globally asymptotically stable equilibrium of \(\dot x=h_\infty(x)\), the gains satisfy \(\sum_na_n=\infty\) and \(\sum_na_n^2<\infty\), and the martingale-difference noise has conditional second moment bounded by \(C(1+\lVert X_n\rVert^2)\), then \(\sup_n\lVert X_n\rVert<\infty\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the rescaled drift at infinity globally attracts toward the origin, standard gain and noise conditions prevent the stochastic recursion from escaping to infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is globally Lipschitz and \(h_c\to h_\infty\) uniformly on compact sets.
The origin is globally asymptotically stable for \(\dot x=h_\infty(x)\).
The gains and martingale noise satisfy the displayed summability and moment conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stochastic-approximation iterates satisfy \(\sup_n\lVert X_n\rVert<\infty\) almost surely.

children.title: Smooth ODE Limits
children.top_down_role: Limiting-flow analysis for recursions with smooth single-valued drift.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth ODE Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ODE-method limit theorem for bounded stochastic-approximation interpolations with a locally Lipschitz mean field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x_{n+1}=x_n+a_n(h(x_n)+M_{n+1}+r_n)\) in \(\mathbb R^d\). Set \(t_0=0\), \(t_n=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}a_k\), let \(X\) be the piecewise-linear interpolation satisfying \(X(t_n)=x_n\), and define \(m(n,s)=\max\{m\ge n:t_m-t_n\le s\}\). Suppose \(a_n>0\), \(a_n\to0\), \(\sum_n a_n=\infty\), \(\sup_n\|x_n\|<\infty\), and \(h:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is locally Lipschitz. Suppose also that, for every \(T>0\) and \(U_{k+1}=M_{k+1}\) or \(U_{k+1}=r_k\), \(\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{0\le s\le T}\|\sum_{k=n}^{m(n,s)-1}a_kU_{k+1}\|=0\). Then every locally uniform subsequential limit of \(X(t_{n_j}+\cdot)\) is a solution of \(\dot x(t)=h(x(t))\) on \([0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every locally uniform limit of a shifted interpolation follows the deterministic mean ODE when the accumulated noise and remainder sums vanish uniformly on each bounded time window.
assumptions_latex: \(a_n>0,\ a_n\to0,\ \sum_n a_n=\infty\)
\(\sup_n\|x_n\|<\infty\), and \(h:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is locally Lipschitz
For each \(T>0\), the weighted noise and remainder sums vanish uniformly over interpolated-time windows of length at most \(T\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X(t_{n_j}+\cdot)\to x(\cdot)\ \Longrightarrow\ \dot x(t)=h(x(t))\text{ for }t\ge0\)

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Valued Differential-Inclusion Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differential-inclusion limit for bounded recursions whose drifts approach a Marchaud set-valued map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathbb R^d\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^d\) have nonempty compact convex values, closed graph, and linear growth, and define \(H^\delta(x)=\{y\in\mathbb R^d:\exists z\in\mathbb R^d,\ \|z-x\|\le\delta,\ \operatorname{dist}(y,H(z))\le\delta\}\). Consider \(x_{n+1}=x_n+a_n(v_n+M_{n+1}+r_n)\), where \(v_n\in H^{\delta_n}(x_n)\), \(\delta_n\ge0\), and \(\delta_n\to0\). Set \(t_0=0\), \(t_n=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}a_k\), let \(X\) be the piecewise-linear interpolation with \(X(t_n)=x_n\), and define \(m(n,s)=\max\{m\ge n:t_m-t_n\le s\}\). Suppose \(a_n>0\), \(a_n\to0\), \(\sum_n a_n=\infty\), \(\sup_n\|x_n\|<\infty\), and, for every \(T>0\) and \(U_{k+1}=M_{k+1}\) or \(U_{k+1}=r_k\), \(\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{0\le s\le T}\|\sum_{k=n}^{m(n,s)-1}a_kU_{k+1}\|=0\). Then every locally uniform subsequential limit \(x\) of \(X(t_{n_j}+\cdot)\) belongs to \(AC_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty);\mathbb R^d)\) and satisfies \(\dot x(t)\in H(x(t))\) for almost every \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Marchaud regularity, vanishing drift enlargement, and negligible accumulated perturbations, every shifted-interpolation limit is a locally absolutely continuous solution of the limiting differential inclusion.

\(a_n>0,\ a_n\to0,\ \sum_n a_n=\infty\), and \(\sup_n\|x_n\|<\infty\)

children.title: Weak-Convergence Method
children.top_down_role: Process-limit analysis for constant, decreasing, and state-dependent gains.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Convergence Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tightness-plus-identification principle for process limits of stochastic-approximation interpolations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^n\) be interpolated or scaled stochastic-approximation processes taking values in a Polish path space. Establish tightness and, for every weakly convergent subsequence \(X^{n_j}\Rightarrow X\), pass the drift, martingale, and negligible-remainder identities to the limit to show that \(X\) solves a specified martingale problem. If that martingale problem has a unique solution law \(P\), then \(X^n\Rightarrow P\). For decreasing or state-dependent gains, the index \(n\) may represent the shifted or scaled recursion; for constant-gain algorithms, it must index a family whose gain parameter tends to zero, together with the corresponding time scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prove process tightness, identify every subsequential limit through a martingale problem, and use uniqueness to obtain full weak convergence; constant-gain limits require a family with gain tending to zero.

Every weak subsequential limit satisfies the designated martingale problem
The limiting martingale problem has unique solution law \(P\) when full-sequence convergence is claimed

children.title: Trajectory Precompactness

knowledge_statements.title: Trajectory Precompactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arzelà–Ascoli criterion for deterministic interpolated trajectories on compact time intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^n:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^d\) be continuous. If, for every \(T>0\), the set \(\{X^n(t):n\ge1,\ 0\le t\le T\}\) is bounded and \(\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\sup_n\sup_{|t-s|\le\delta,\,s,t\le T}\|X^n(t)-X^n(s)\|=0\), then \(\{X^n\}\) is relatively compact in \(C([0,\infty);\mathbb R^d)\) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact intervals. Consequently, every sequence contains a subsequence converging uniformly on each bounded time interval to a continuous trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform boundedness and equicontinuity on each finite horizon make the interpolated trajectories precompact under locally uniform convergence.
assumptions_latex: The trajectories \(X^n\) are continuous
Their ranges are uniformly bounded on every finite horizon
They are equicontinuous uniformly in \(n\) on every finite horizon
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{X^n\}\) is relatively compact in \(C_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty);\mathbb R^d)\)

notation.meaning: continuous-path space with locally uniform topology

children.title: Process-Level Tightness

knowledge_statements.title: Process-Level Tightness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-containment and modulus criterion for tightness of continuous stochastic processes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^n\) be random elements of \(C([0,T];\mathbb R^d)\), and define \(w_T(x,\delta)=\sup\{\|x(t)-x(s)\|:0\le s,t\le T,\ |t-s|\le\delta\}\). The family \(\{X^n\}\) is tight if, for every \(\eta>0\), there is \(K<\infty\) with \(\sup_n\mathbb P(\sup_{t\le T}\|X^n(t)\|>K)<\eta\), and \(\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\sup_n\mathbb P(w_T(X^n,\delta)>\eta)=0\). If these conditions hold for every \(T>0\), the laws are tight in the locally uniform continuous-path space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact containment and uniformly vanishing path oscillations imply tightness of the process laws on continuous-path space.
assumptions_latex: \(X^n\) has continuous paths on each finite horizon
The compact-containment bound holds
The probabilistic modulus-of-continuity bound holds
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\mathcal L(X^n)\}\) is tight in \(C_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty);\mathbb R^d)\)

notation.meaning: path modulus of continuity over horizon T

knowledge_statements.title: Subsequence Limit Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification of weak subsequential limits by integral equations or martingale problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(X^n\) is tight in a Polish path space. For each subsequence choose a further subsequence with \(X^{n_j}\Rightarrow X\). If the recursion's drift, quadratic-variation, and remainder relations pass to the limit so that every such \(X\) solves the same limiting integral equation or martingale problem, then every weak accumulation point belongs to that solution class. If the limiting problem has a unique law \(P\), the full sequence converges weakly to \(P\); without uniqueness, tightness yields only subsequential convergence to the set of solution laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pass recursion identities to each weak limit; uniqueness of the resulting limiting problem upgrades subsequential convergence to full weak convergence.

Drift, variation, and remainder identities are stable under subsequential limits
The limiting problem has unique law \(P\) for full-sequence convergence

knowledge_statements.title: Almost-Sure Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robbins–Monro convergence to a globally asymptotically stable equilibrium under bounded iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{n+1}=x_n+a_n(h(x_n)+M_{n+1}+r_n)\) in \(\mathbb R^d\). Assume \(a_n>0\), \(\sum_n a_n=\infty\), \(\sum_n a_n^2<\infty\); \(M_{n+1}\) is a martingale difference with uniformly bounded conditional second moment along the bounded iterates; and \(r_n\to0\) almost surely. If \(h\) is locally Lipschitz and the ODE \(\dot x=h(x)\) has a unique globally asymptotically stable equilibrium \(x^*\), then \(x_n\to x^*\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Square-summable noise gains, bounded iterates, vanishing bias, and global ODE stability imply pathwise convergence to the equilibrium.
assumptions_latex: \(\sum_n a_n=\infty\) and \(\sum_n a_n^2<\infty\)
The iterates are almost surely bounded and the martingale differences have bounded conditional second moments
\(r_n\to0\) almost surely, and \(x^*\) is globally asymptotically stable for \(\dot x=h(x)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\lim_{n\to\infty}x_n=x^*)=1\)

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Distribution Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central limit theorem for a locally linear Robbins–Monro recursion with gain \(a/n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x_n\to x^*\) in probability and \(x_{n+1}=x_n+(a/n)(h(x_n)+M_{n+1}+r_n)\), where \(h(x^*)=0\), \(h(x)=J(x-x^*)+o(\|x-x^*\|)\), and \(aJ+I/2\) is Hurwitz. Assume the martingale noise satisfies a conditional Lindeberg condition and its conditional covariance converges in probability to \(\Sigma\), while \(\sqrt n\,r_n\to0\) in probability. Then \(\sqrt n(x_n-x^*)\Rightarrow N(0,V)\), where \(V\) is the unique positive semidefinite solution of \((aJ+I/2)V+V(aJ^{\mathsf T}+I/2)+a^2\Sigma=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local linear stability and regular martingale noise yield a Gaussian root-n error limit with covariance determined by a Lyapunov equation.
assumptions_latex: \(x_n\to x^*\) in probability and \(aJ+I/2\) is Hurwitz
The martingale array satisfies conditional covariance convergence and a conditional Lindeberg condition
\(\sqrt n\,r_n\to0\) in probability
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqrt n(x_n-x^*)\Rightarrow N(0,V)\)

children.title: Convergence-Rate Results

knowledge_statements.title: Convergence-Rate Results
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root-mean-square iteration rate derived from bounded normalized stochastic-approximation errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_n\) converge to \(x^*\), and suppose the normalized errors \(Z_n=\sqrt n(x_n-x^*)\) satisfy \(\sup_n\mathbb E\|Z_n\|^2<C\). Then \(\mathbb E\|x_n-x^*\|^2\le C/n\), so the root-mean-square error is at most \(\sqrt{C/n}\). Consequently, in the one-simulation-oracle-call-per-iteration model, achieving \((\mathbb E\|x_n-x^*\|^2)^{1/2}\le\varepsilon\) requires at most \(N(\varepsilon)=\lceil C\varepsilon^{-2}\rceil\) iterations and oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded root-n normalized errors give mean-square rate O(1/n) and RMS oracle complexity O(epsilon to the minus two).
assumptions_latex: \(\sup_n\mathbb E\|\sqrt n(x_n-x^*)\|^2\le C<\infty\)
Each iteration uses one simulation-oracle call
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E\|x_n-x^*\|^2\le C/n\) and \(N(\varepsilon)\le\lceil C\varepsilon^{-2}\rceil\)

knowledge_statements.title: Escape from Nonoptimal Traps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure escape from an isolated strict saddle under persistent local noise excitation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider stochastic gradient descent \(x_{n+1}=x_n-a_n(\nabla f(x_n)+M_{n+1})\), where \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable near an isolated critical point \(x^s\) and \(\nabla^2f(x^s)\) has a negative eigenvalue. Suppose \(a_n>0\), \(\sum_n a_n=\infty\), \(\sum_n a_n^2<\infty\), the martingale-difference noise has bounded conditional second moments, and its conditional variance is uniformly positive in every unstable direction near \(x^s\). Then the probability that the iterates remain eventually in every neighborhood of \(x^s\), equivalently converge to \(x^s\), is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent noise in unstable directions prevents stochastic gradient descent from converging to an isolated strict saddle.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(x^s\) is an isolated strict saddle
\(\sum_n a_n=\infty\) and \(\sum_n a_n^2<\infty\)
Noise has bounded second moments and uniformly excites unstable directions near \(x^s\)

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable-Limit Avoidance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvergence to a linearly unstable equilibrium of a smooth stochastic-approximation mean flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{n+1}=x_n+a_n(h(x_n)+M_{n+1}+r_n)\), and let \(x^u\) satisfy \(h(x^u)=0\). Assume \(h\) is continuously differentiable near \(x^u\), its Jacobian \(Dh(x^u)\) has an eigenvalue with positive real part, the gains satisfy \(\sum_n a_n=\infty\) and \(\sum_n a_n^2<\infty\), and \(r_n\) is asymptotically negligible. If the martingale noise has bounded conditional second moments and uniformly nonzero conditional variance on the unstable subspace near \(x^u\), then \(\mathbb P(x_n\to x^u)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic approximation cannot converge with positive probability to a linearly unstable equilibrium when noise persistently excites its unstable subspace.
